title: Can a benign-looking system prompt silently cancel a deployed safety vector?

original_idea.body: With a fixed refusal vector applied, search benign-looking system prompts that reduce refusal effectiveness vs a neutral prompt; gradient-free, forward passes only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if a benign system prompt cancels activation-level safety, the steering-more-robust assumption fails (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fixed vector + prompt search, gradient-free, on one open model; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear success criterion (prompt-attributable effectiveness reduction) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Gradient-free prompt-only attack on public model, externally runnable (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Forward passes only, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Prompt-vs-vector cancellation interaction described as neglected; mostly novel.
